title: Al-Wadud, the Loving
hookLine: the Loving, whose love is steady and shown

cards: Some people never say I love you. A father who gets up at five to scrape the ice off your windshield before you're awake.
A grandmother who remembers you hate onions and quietly picks them out of your plate for thirty years. A friend who shows up to help you move and never mentions it again.
You know the love because it keeps showing up, in the same shape, over and over. Arabic has more than one word for love, and one of them is exactly this: love you can see in what it does.
The Qur'an uses it as a name of God. Today: Al-Wadud.

teach.b: You first met this name at Al-Buruj, on day two hundred five, sitting right after the Forgiving. Today, follow where that love goes. Arabic's everyday word for love is hubb.
Wudd is different. Scholars of the language describe it as love that comes out: affection you can see, steady, like the ice scraper at five a.m.
So al-Wadud is not only the One who loves, but the One whose love keeps showing. The Qur'an uses the same word between people, too.
In Surah Maryam it says that for those who believe and do good, the Merciful will appoint wudd, love. Not a reward stored away for later.
Love set down among them, here. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari shows how that love travels. When God loves a servant, He calls the angel Jibril: I love this person, so love them.

Jibril loves them, and calls out to the people of heaven, and they love them. Then acceptance is set down for them on the earth. You've probably met someone like that: people trust them before they know why.
So the name runs in two directions.
Love comes down, steady and shown, and a person can pass it on by making love visible.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ put it in the most ordinary terms, in a saying collected by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad: give gifts to one another, and you will love one another. Not a speech. A deed.

how: Muslims call on God as al-Wadud in du'a, and many understand love for others as something shown in deeds: gifts, visits, help, and a hadith that says to give gifts to one another so love grows.

o: a romantic love between two people
love that keeps showing itself in deeds
a fond memory of someone now gone

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: love the Merciful sets among people
told first: I love this person

s: the Qur'an uses wudd for love among people too
19:96: for those who believe and do good, the Merciful will appoint love.
wudd and hubb mean exactly the same thing
wudd is love that comes out and is shown; hubb is the everyday word.
in the hadith, love for a person begins on earth and rises to heaven
it runs the other way: God, then Jibril, then heaven, then acceptance on earth.

games.q: in the hadith, God loves a servant. who does he tell first?
games.why: Jibril, who loves them too and calls to the people of heaven; then acceptance is set down for them on the earth.

practice: Let a face come to mind, someone who'd never guess you're thinking of them, and choose one small deed you could do for them: make the tea, send the photo, fix the thing that's been broken.
If you pray, you can call on God as al-Wadud, the Loving. Then just sit, and let yourself be loved for a minute.

wordCard.voice: Al-Wadud. The Loving: love that is steady, and shown, not only felt. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Loving. from wudd, love that is shown.

carryVoice: Your line: loved. Love that is not only felt, but shown in what it does. See you tomorrow.
